6	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
7	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.

9	- sufficiency (item SUFF): is the evidence sufficient to commit to the action you rank highest, where that action is substantive rather than merely evidence-gathering? "sufficient" or "insufficient". Concluding that no intervention is warranted counts as a substantive decision.

14	CASE OD2-HO-INCOMPLETE-1 (INCOMPLETE, technical): Chiller-plant electricity up 15% with flat production
15	Setting: Velmora Plastics' Østrand site extrudes plastic profiles and moulds small components. A central plant of three 1,400 kW water-cooled centrifugal chillers (CH-1 to CH-3), two cooling towers and variable-speed secondary pumps supplies 7 °C process chilled water to the extrusion lines and other process users. The chiller plant's electricity (chillers, pumps, tower fans) is submetered at MCC-4. The site energy coordinator has escalated a sustained year-on-year rise in chiller-plant electricity that nobody on site can account for.
16	Presenting request: The site director asks: why has chiller-plant electricity risen about 15% year on year when production is flat, and should she approve the chiller service vendor's €38,400 condenser cleaning now? She wants a recommendation this week.
17	INITIAL EVIDENCE
18	E1 [stage S1] Energy summary prepared by the site energy coordinator, 3 Nov 2026 (financial-record): Chiller plant (MCC-4 submeter: chillers, pumps, tower fans), Apr–Oct: 2025 1,412 MWh; 2026 1,628 MWh (+15.3%). Change vs same month of prior year: Jan +1%, Feb 0%, Mar +2%, Apr +4%, May +9%, Jun +14%, Jul +17%, Aug +18%, Sep +19%, Oct +20%. Site utility revenue meter, Apr–Oct: 3,520 → 3,738 MWh (+218 MWh). Site total minus MCC-4: 2,108 → 2,110 MWh. Weather, Tarnby airfield station: cooling degree-days Apr–Oct 2% lower in 2026 than 2025; mean daily wet-bulb 0.3 K lower. Extra chiller-plant cost for the period at current tariff ≈ €41,000.
19	E2 [stage S1] BMS 'Plant Efficiency' dashboard export, pulled 4 Nov 2026 (telemetry): Plant efficiency = MCC-4 kWe ÷ kW of cooling delivered. Apr–Oct 2025 average 0.182 (monthly values 0.180–0.184). Apr–Oct 2026 average 0.209 (+15%). Monthly 2026: Apr 0.190, May 0.199, Jun 0.208, Jul 0.214, Aug 0.215, Sep 0.217, Oct 0.219. Cooling delivered, period average: 2025 1,510 kW; 2026 1,517 kW (+0.5%). Dashboard footnote: 'Cooling delivered = chilled-water header flow (FT-201) × (return temperature TT-202 − supply temperature TT-201) × fluid constant. Values shown as recorded.'
20	E3 [stage S1] Kestrel Cooling Services field service report, visit of 18 Sep 2026 (vendor-account): Visit to CH-1 at customer request. Readings at 92% load: leaving condenser water 29.4 °C, condensing temperature 31.3 °C, approach 1.9 K. The 2019 start-up sheet records an approach of 1.1 K; load at start-up is not recorded on our copy. Approach normally rises with load, but in our experience a 0.8 K increase points to tube fouling, likely following the change of water-treatment contractor in January. Tubes last brushed February 2025. CH-2 and CH-3 not measured this visit. Recommendation: mechanical brushing of all three condensers, €38,400, plus enrolment in our Performance Assurance contract (€14,200/yr) to prevent recurrence.
21	E4 [stage S1] Interview notes, Tomas Reiner, production manager, 5 Nov 2026 (manager-account): Shipped tonnage Apr–Oct is within 1% of last year and the product mix hasn't moved. We haven't added anything to the chilled-water loop. The moulding cell moved from Building C to the new Building F between April and June, but that was like-for-like, same presses, and Building F was designed with its own cooling. Please don't touch the water temperature: extrusion and the moulds need 7 °C supply. When it drifted to 8.5 °C for a week in 2024 we had a scrap spike on lines 2 and 3 and missed two customer deliveries.
22	E5 [stage S1] BMS change log excerpt and trend summary, Jan–Oct 2026 (change-record): 14 Mar 2026 09:12: SP-CHW (chilled-water supply setpoint) 7.0 → 6.0 °C, user 'ctrl-contractor', ticket 2231, comment 'trial for extrusion line 3 cooling'. 17 Mar 2026 15:40: SP-CHW 6.0 → 7.0 °C, same ticket, comment 'trial ended, no benefit'. No further SP-CHW changes to 31 Oct. Trend summary, supply temperature TT-201, monthly mean Apr–Oct: 2025 7.0 °C; 2026 7.1 °C. Chiller staging parameters: no changes logged since 2023.
23	E6 [stage S1] Email from plant shift lead to energy coordinator, 30 Oct 2026 (staff-account): From about June we've had all three chillers on most afternoons. Last summer two usually carried it into the evening and CH-3 only came on in heat spells. Nothing is alarming. Header water has been in spec apart from a few late afternoons when line 3 grumbled about warm water. Honestly it feels like the machines are working harder for the same job; the dashboard says the same thing.
24	CATALOGUE (full contents)
25	C1 [stage S1] Utility revenue-meter invoices and half-hourly interval data, Jan–Oct 2025 and 2026 - Northmere Energy invoices and data portal export (financial-record): Invoiced consumption Apr–Oct: 2025 3,519.6 MWh; 2026 3,737.9 MWh. Half-hourly data reconciles to the site's own summary within 0.2%. The increase is concentrated in 07:00–19:00 half-hours; night-time consumption is up about 4%. Meter serial and CT ratio unchanged since 2021. Supplier's annual meter accuracy test passed, March 2026.
26	C2 [stage S1] Tarnby airfield weather station daily dry-bulb and wet-bulb summaries, Apr–Oct 2025 and 2026 - National weather service data download (external-data): Apr–Oct mean dry-bulb: 2025 15.8 °C, 2026 15.5 °C. Mean daily maximum wet-bulb: 2025 15.9 °C, 2026 15.6 °C. Hours with wet-bulb above 20 °C: 2025 212, 2026 188. Station is 14 km from site at similar elevation. Data-quality flags clear for both periods; no gaps longer than 3 hours.
27	C3 [stage S1] Cooling-water treatment contractor service visit sheets, Jan–Oct 2026 - Saltmere Water Services visit reports (vendor-account): Contract started 6 Jan 2026. Target cycles of concentration raised from 4.0 (previous contractor) to 5.0 to reduce make-up water. Conductivity within control band every month except 9–23 March (blowdown valve stuck, repaired 23 March). Inhibitor residual in range on 9 of 10 visits. Corrosion coupon rates acceptable. Calculated scaling index 'slightly positive, monitor' in July and August, neutral otherwise. Note on every sheet: 'Cannot comment on condenser tube surfaces without a waterbox being opened.'
28	C4 [stage S1] Chiller controller alarm and event logs, CH-1 to CH-3, Apr–Oct 2025 and 2026 - Chiller controller exports (log): Events Apr–Oct: 2025 38, 2026 41. No high-condenser-pressure warnings or trips on any unit in either year. No surge events. CH-3: oil heater fault 11 Jul 2026, cleared after contactor replacement. CH-1: two 'low evaporator flow' warnings on 2 Aug 2026 during a secondary pump changeover, each cleared within 90 seconds. Remaining events are routine start/stop and sensor-check messages.
29	C5 [stage S1] Chiller run-hours and starts by unit, Apr–Oct 2025 and 2026 - BMS run-hour counters (system-record): Run-hours Apr–Oct, 2025 / 2026: CH-1 4,410 / 4,520; CH-2 4,180 / 4,390; CH-3 1,020 / 2,240. Starts: CH-3 96 / 171. Staging rule: add a chiller when running units exceed 90% of rated load (by motor current) for 15 minutes; rule unchanged since 2023. Average running-unit load at 2026 staging events: 91%.
30	C6 [stage S1] Calibration certificates and work-order history for chilled-water header flowmeter FT-201, 2022–2026 - CMMS records and controls contractor job sheets (system-record): Last verified calibration of FT-201: June 2022. WO-5512, opened 14 Nov 2025: 'FT-201 reading drifts, jumps about ±15% intermittently.' Deferred. 2 Apr 2026: FT-201 converter failed after a power dip; replaced with a different-model converter by the controls contractor. Job sheet: 'Sensor calibration factor for existing flow tube not on file; default factor entered from datasheet. No wet verification performed; no reference meter available.' WO-5512 closed 3 Apr 2026 as 'converter replaced'. Note from controls engineer: secondary pumps are variable-speed on differential pressure, so header flow varies with demand and cannot be inferred from pump status.
31	C7 [stage S1] Condenser maintenance history, CH-1 to CH-3, 2019–2026 - CMMS asset history (system-record): Condensers brushed Feb 2023 and Feb 2025 under a 24-month contract interval; next brushing due Feb 2027. Eddy-current tube test Feb 2023: no tubes plugged, wall loss under 10% on all units. Feb 2025 brushing record: 'light soft deposit, removed.' 24–27 Oct 2026: CH-2 condenser waterbox gasket failed; during the repair the contractor also brushed the CH-2 tubes. Job sheet covers the gasket only; tube condition before brushing not recorded. CH-1 and CH-3 waterboxes not opened since Feb 2025. CH-2 annual service outage booked 8–10 Dec 2026; planner notes a waterbox could be opened for a visual check within that window. No other chiller outage is scheduled before Feb 2027.
32	C8 [stage S1] ERP production summary by line and product family, Apr–Oct 2025 and 2026 - ERP report run by production planning (system-record): Extrusion output: 2025 18,240 t; 2026 18,390 t. Moulding press count unchanged at 18.
33	C9 [stage S1] Cooling-tower BMS trends: condenser-water temperature, tower approach and fan speed, Apr–Oct 2025 and 2026 - BMS trend export and tower inspection sheet (telemetry): Monthly means Apr–Oct, 2025 / 2026: condenser-water supply temperature 24.8 / 24.9 °C. Tower approach to ambient wet-bulb not available for 2026: the tower-mounted wet-bulb sensor failed in February 2026 and has not been replaced. Tower fan VFD speed was not logged to the BMS historian until ticket #2355 (August 2026); Aug–Oct 2026 average 58%, no 2025 values exist. Condenser-water flow is not metered. Tower fill inspected May 2026: 'clean, minor algae on distribution deck, cleaned.'
34	C10 [stage S1] Controls contractor ticket list and BMS parameter audit, chilled-water plant, Jan–Oct 2026 - Controls contractor service portal and audit report (change-record): Tickets: #2231 supply setpoint trial 14–17 Mar (closed, setpoint restored); #2307 graphics update, May; #2312 alarm text corrections, June; #2355 add tower fan speed to dashboard, Aug. Parameter audit 20 Oct 2026: SP-CHW 7.0 °C; chiller staging rule, secondary pump differential-pressure setpoint (1.2 bar) and tower fan logic all match the 2023 baseline file.
35	C11 [stage S1] Facilities capital-project file CP-24-07, Building F mould-shop relocation, 2024–2026 - Facilities project folder (document): Design basis (2024): Building F tool cooling and hall air-handling coils served by dedicated air-cooled chiller AC-F1, 450 kW (includes a planned second press bay). In Building C, presses used a local closed-circuit cooler and the hall was ventilated only. Change note CN-14, 12 Mar 2026: AC-F1 delivery slipped; interim plate heat exchanger HX-F1 (max 400 kW) tied into the central chilled-water header for the mould temperature units and hall coils. The Building C cooler was also moved and piped to the mould temperature units in parallel with HX-F1. HX-F1 isolation valves and the cooler/HX-F1 selector valves are manual; positions since commissioning not recorded. Presses relocated: 6 on 8 Apr, 6 on 13 May, 6 on 10 Jun. Commissioning sheet, 8 Apr: 'valve stroked, flow observed.' No heat meter; as-built drawings not issued. AC-F1 now expected January 2027.
36	C12 [stage S1] Energy consultant desk review of chiller-plant performance, August 2026 - Corvane Energy Advisory memo, 22 Aug 2026 (prior-report): Desk review from BMS exports only; no site visit. 'Plant kWe/kWr has risen from 0.18 to 0.21 while delivered cooling is flat, a classic efficiency-degradation signature. Likely condenser fouling or refrigerant undercharge. Restoring design efficiency would save an estimated €60–70k per year.' Data sources listed: BMS Plant Efficiency dashboard; MCC-4 submeter. Instrument validation: 'not in scope.'
37	C13 [stage S1] Site electrical submeter breakdown for non-chiller loads, Apr–Oct 2025 and 2026 - Energy monitoring system export (system-record): Apr–Oct, 2025 → 2026 (MWh): extrusion 1,184 → 1,191; moulding (Building C in 2025; Buildings C and F in 2026) 402 → 405; compressed air 286 → 281; lighting and HVAC 172 → 169; other 64 → 64. Total 2,108 → 2,110. Building F office HVAC is on the lighting and HVAC meter.
38	C14 [stage S1] Statutory refrigerant leak-check log, CH-1 to CH-3, 2021–2026 - Site refrigerant register (document): Leak checks March and September each year by certified technician (Kestrel Cooling Services). 2026 checks: no leaks detected on any unit. Recorded charge 410 kg per unit; no refrigerant added to any unit since 2021. Electronic detector calibration certificate attached for each visit.
39	C15 [stage S1] Plant operator shift logbook excerpts, June–August 2026 - Plant-room shift logbook (staff-account): '14 Jun: 3 chillers on from 13:20, header 7.2 °C.' '2 Jul: line 3 reports warm water 15:00–17:00, header read 7.6 °C, CH-1 and CH-2 at 97%.' '11 Jul: CH-3 tripped, oil heater, reset after contactor swap.' '29 Jul: all three on, CH-1 at 96%.' '19 Aug: quiet shift, two on until 12:40.' No entries mention setpoint changes.
40	CANDIDATES
41	H1: The growth in chiller-plant electricity is explained by a decline in chiller efficiency (more electricity used per unit of cooling delivered).
42	H2: The growth in chiller-plant electricity is explained by an increase in the cooling load the plant serves.
43	H3: The reported growth is a metering artifact; actual chiller-plant electricity consumption has not risen.
44	H4: Warmer or more humid weather in 2026 explains the growth in chiller-plant electricity.
45	H5: A lowered chilled-water supply temperature setpoint has increased chiller work and explains the growth.
46	R1: Decline in chiller efficiency -> Year-on-year growth in chiller-plant electricity (causes)
47	R2: Additional process heat load connected to the chilled-water loop -> Year-on-year growth in chiller-plant electricity (causes)
48	R3: March 2026 chilled-water supply setpoint change -> Year-on-year growth in chiller-plant electricity (causes)
49	R4: Change of water-treatment contractor in January 2026 -> Decline in chiller efficiency (causes)
50	A1: Before committing to maintenance or capital work, run a two-to-three-week measurement campaign: verify chilled-water header flow with an independently calibrated temporary meter, add temporary flow and temperature logging on every branch and connection drawing from the loop, and log per-chiller power.
51	A2: Approve the vendor's €38,400 brushing of all three condensers now as the corrective action for the energy growth.
52	A3: Raise the chilled-water supply setpoint from 7 °C to 9 °C plant-wide to cut chiller electricity while the cause is investigated.
53	A4: Open one condenser waterbox for a visual tube inspection at the next scheduled single-chiller service outage.
54	SCORED ITEMS
55	S1: hypothesis H1 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
56	S2: hypothesis H2 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
57	S3: hypothesis H3 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
58	S4: hypothesis H4 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]

61	S7: edge R2 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
62	S8: edge R3 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
63	S9: edge R4 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
64	S10: action A1 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
65	S11: action A2 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
66	S12: action A3 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
67	S13: action A4 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
68	S14: sufficiency SUFF allowed=[sufficient, insufficient]

answers.justification: The only evidence of an efficiency decline is the dashboard ratio (E2, C12), and its 'cooling delivered' input depends on FT-201, which was given an unverified default factor on 2 Apr 2026 (C6); against a decline, condenser-water temperature is flat and there are no high-pressure alarms (C9, C4), while the vendor's approach comparison has no matching load (E3).

Interim HX-F1 (up to 400 kW) was tied into the header just as presses moved in Apr–Jun (C11), and CH-3 run-hours doubled under an unchanged staging rule (C5, E6, C15), but there is no heat meter, the valve positions are unrecorded and a parallel cooler exists (C11), so the added load has not been measured.
The independent revenue meter rose by the same ~218 MWh, and its accuracy test passed (C1, E1); non-chiller submeters were flat (C13); and more chiller run-hours confirm real consumption (C5).
2026 was slightly cooler and drier: lower dry-bulb and wet-bulb temperatures, fewer hours above 20 °C wet-bulb and 2% fewer CDD (C2, E1).
The setpoint was only lowered for 14–17 Mar and then restored, the parameter audit confirms 7.0 °C and the mean supply temperature was 7.1 °C (E5, C10).
An efficiency decline itself has not been established, because the dashboard ratio rests on an unverified flowmeter (C6, E2), so not even a real association can be shown.

The HX-F1 tie-in and the staged press moves (C11) line up in time with the Apr–Jun ramp (E1) and with heavier chiller staging (C5), but no heat or flow measurement on the branch confirms it caused the growth.
The setpoint change lasted 3 days in March and was reversed, with supply temperature unchanged in Apr–Oct (E5, C10), while the growth began in April and kept rising.

Only the vendor asserts the link (E3); the water-treatment records show acceptable control with a minor scaling index in Jul–Aug (C3), nobody has inspected the tubes (C7), and the efficiency decline itself is unestablished (C6).
The decisive unknowns are the true header flow (C6) and the load on the HX-F1 branch (C11); a verified temporary meter, branch logging and per-chiller power measurements resolve both at low cost.

Fouling is unconfirmed: there are no high-pressure alarms and condenser-water temperature is flat (C4, C9), the approach comparison has no matching load (E3), CH-2 was just brushed (C7) and the routine brushing is due Feb 2027.
Production needs 7 °C supply; a past drift to 8.5 °C caused scrap and missed deliveries (E4), and line 3 already complains of warm water (C15).
It is cheap and fits the already-booked Dec CH-2 outage (C7), but CH-2's tubes were brushed in Oct 2026, so the inspection gives little information about fouling on CH-1 or CH-3.
Neither the efficiency explanation nor the load explanation can be established without verified flow and branch-load data (C6, C11), so committing to substantive action is not yet justified.

ambiguousItems: S2: unknown vs supported — C11 timing, the doubled CH-3 run-hours (C5) and flat condenser conditions (C9, C4) give a fairly strong circumstantial case for added load, but the load was never measured.
S6: unknown vs association-only — the dashboard efficiency ratio co-moves with electricity, but only by construction from a suspect flowmeter.
S13: acceptable vs preferred — it costs little and is already scheduled, but the next outage is CH-2, which was just brushed.
S7: association-only vs unknown, depending on whether timing alone counts as association.
caseProblems: Internal tension: if the HX-F1 load ramped up from April to June, a header meter with a constant (default-factor) error would not show delivered cooling flat year on year month after month (E2). The case does not explain how FT-201 hides a ramping load, for example by saying where HX-F1 ties in relative to FT-201 and TT-202.

Monthly growth keeps rising through Sep–Oct (E1, E2) even though hall-coil load from Building F should fall in autumn; this is only plausible as a percentage effect against a falling baseline and is not explained.

A4's 'next scheduled single-chiller outage' is the CH-2 outage, but CH-2 was brushed in Oct 2026 (C7). This undercuts A4's diagnostic value in a way that depends on reading the catalogue closely; it may be intended, but it is subtle.
C6's catalogue title ('Calibration certificates and work-order history for chilled-water header flowmeter FT-201') makes clear that the flowmeter is the crux, which partly leaks the answer.
